Input / Action: "<script>alert(1)</script> we need a database for user records" typed into the requirement box, then a real DOM-XSS payload (<img src=x onerror=...>) tested for actual execution
Expected Result: User text is always rendered as plain text everywhere it appears, never as live HTML/DOM
Actual Result (live browser): THE HISTORY SIDEBAR'S .shi-label SPAN RENDERS RAW REQUIREMENT TEXT VIA innerHTML, UNESCAPED. Confirmed a real <img src=x onerror=...> payload EXECUTED (window.__xssProof flipped to true) the moment the entry rendered in the "Recent" sidebar. Visually corroborated — a broken image icon appears inline in the history list.
Notes: NEW finding, not from the external report. This is a real client-side script-injection bug: renderSidebarHistory()'s .shi-label building the entry via a template-literal into innerHTML instead of textContent. The title="" attribute on the same element correctly HTML-escapes (proving the fix is a one-line change, not a redesign) — only the visible label span doesn't. Practical exploit path: the app's own "Paste your own description" mode explicitly invites pasting external documents (job specs, PRDs) into the requirement box — a malicious pasted doc would silently execute in the user's own session the next time the sidebar renders. Recommend fixing immediately.
